hypothesis: Geospatial mHealth data tracking of patient travel time to clinics predicts lower adherence to follow-up appointments in rural cohorts.
research_question: To what extent does real-time geospatial tracking of travel burden predict appointment non-adherence in rural health services?
independent_variable: Geospatial travel time data derived from mHealth GPS logs
target_population: Rural patients with chronic diseases requiring frequent clinical monitoring
potential_contribution: Identifies high-risk patients for remote monitoring interventions based on objective physical accessibility barriers.

hypothesis: Mobile-delivered remote patient monitoring (RPM) reduces the frequency of emergency department (ED) visits for rural patients by improving early detection of clinical deterioration.
research_question: Can mHealth-based remote monitoring reduce reliance on emergency services by improving accessibility to proactive rural health management?
potential_contribution: Demonstrates a shift from reactive emergency care to proactive, accessible rural health management via mHealth.

hypothesis: The integration of asynchronous mHealth-based tele-triage algorithms significantly increases the utilization of primary care services among rural populations compared to standard referral pathways.
research_question: Does the implementation of an asynchronous mHealth tele-triage system improve health services accessibility for rural residents?
target_population: Rural residents with chronic conditions residing in medically underserved areas
potential_contribution: Provides a scalable, evidence-based mechanism to bridge the rural-urban health services accessibility gap using existing mobile infrastructure.
